section: River water sharing disputes - Krishna and Godavari; KWDT-I and II, GWDT, Apex Council, Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards
subsections: Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956 and Article 262

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Project — River

1. Pothireddypadu Head Regulator/Rayalaseema Lift — Krishna
2. Kaleshwaram — Godavari
3. Pattiseema and Polavaram — Godavari
4. Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar Link — Godavari to Krishna to Penna
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar Link envisages diversion from the Godavari through the Krishna basin to the Penna basin.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure river-project pairs and eliminate codes that omit a correct pair.

accepted.s: With reference to the Pothireddypadu Head Regulator/Rayalaseema Lift project, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh objects that the project lacks CWC and KRMB clearance.
Karnataka has sought national-project status for the project.
Odisha objects to submergence caused by the project.
Telangana objects that Srisailam is mainly a power project.
accepted.x: Telangana’s objection is that Srisailam is mainly a power project. The project was built by Andhra Pradesh on the Krishna River.
accepted.tq: Test the objecting State and its specific ground rather than merely identifying the project.

accepted.s: Which of the following projects is associated with Telangana as the builder and with objections from Andhra Pradesh regarding the absence of CWC/KRMB clearance?
accepted.x: Palamuru-Rangareddy and Dindi are Telangana projects on the Krishna River. Andhra Pradesh has objected to the absence of clearance from the Central Water Commission and the Krishna River Management Board.
accepted.tq: Use the builder-and-objection combination to distinguish closely related inter-State projects.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Karnataka has also complained about the Palamuru-Rangareddy and Dindi projects.
2. Telangana wants national-project status for Kaleshwaram.
3. Andhra Pradesh has sought clearances for Kaleshwaram.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Karnataka has also complained about the Palamuru-Rangareddy and Dindi projects, while the two States have expressed the stated positions regarding Kaleshwaram.
accepted.tq: Separate each State’s position on different projects before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s:
Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?

Project — Objection

1. Pattiseema and Polavaram — Submergence concerns of Telangana and Odisha
2. Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar Link — Andhra Pradesh would exceed its Krishna share
3. Kaleshwaram — Telangana objects to the lack of any Krishna basin diversion
4. Palamuru-Rangareddy and Dindi — Absence of CWC/KRMB clearance
accepted.x: Statement 3 is not correctly matched. In relation to Kaleshwaram, Andhra Pradesh sought clearances and Telangana wanted national-project status; the stated objection about exceeding the Krishna share concerns the Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar Link.
accepted.tq: Find the project whose objection has been transferred from a neighbouring project.

accepted.s: The proposed Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar Link is intended to carry water through which sequence of river basins?
accepted.x: The project, earlier referred to as Polavaram-Banakacherla Link, is planned as a Godavari to Krishna to Penna transfer.
accepted.tq: Read the flow sequence from source river to intermediate and destination river.

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh plans to divert how much Polavaram flood water through the Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar Link?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh plans to divert 200 TMC of Polavaram flood water through the proposed link.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the proposed diversion quantity from project-capacity and tribunal-share figures.

accepted.s: The proposed diversion of Polavaram flood water is expected to benefit approximately how many people and how much area?
accepted.x: The proposed link is expected to benefit about 80 lakh people and 7.5 lakh acres through reservoirs at Bollapalli and Banakacherla.
accepted.tq: Keep the population figure and irrigated-area figure paired; do not reverse their units.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding recent developments concerning the Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar Link is correct?
o: Telangana withdrew its Supreme Court petition against the link, and a Jal Shakti committee under the CWC Chairman first met on 30 January 2026.
Telangana withdrew its petition before the Southern Zonal Council, and the committee was headed by the Union Home Minister.
The Supreme Court constituted the committee, which first met on 13 January 2026.
Andhra Pradesh withdrew its Supreme Court petition, and the committee first met on 31 August 2026.
accepted.x: Telangana withdrew its Supreme Court petition against the link. A Jal Shakti committee under the Chairman of the Central Water Commission first met on 30 January 2026.
accepted.tq: Match the correct authority, forum and date instead of relying on the general controversy.

accepted.s: Veligonda Phase-I, inaugurated on 31 August 2026, is associated with which of the following?
o: Krishna to Penna transfer, 120 TMC and 80 lakh people
Godavari to Krishna transfer, 200 TMC and 7.5 lakh acres
Krishna to Nallamala Sagar transfer, 10.7 TMC and 1.19 lakh acres
Godavari to Penna transfer, 10.7 TMC and 7.5 lakh acres
accepted.x: Veligonda Phase-I was inaugurated on 31 August 2026 and involves a Krishna to Nallamala Sagar transfer, with 10.7 TMC and 1.19 lakh acres associated with it.
accepted.tq: Combine the inauguration date with the project’s route, quantity and area figures.

accepted.s: Article 262(1) of the Constitution empowers Parliament to provide by law for:
o: Transfer of all State rivers to the Union List
Automatic allocation of river water by the Supreme Court
Appointment of all members of State water tribunals by the President
accepted.x: Article 262(1) enables Parliament to provide by law for the adjudication of disputes relating to the use, distribution or control of waters of inter-State rivers or river valleys.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific constitutional power rather than an associated institutional consequence.
accepted.sec: Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956 and Article 262

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 262:
1. Clause (1) concerns parliamentary provision for adjudicating inter-State river disputes.
2. Clause (2) permits Parliament to bar the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and other courts over such disputes.
3. Clause (2) itself establishes the Inter-State River Water Disputes Tribunal.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Article 262(2) permits exclusion of court jurisdiction, but the tribunals are created through legislation such as the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, not directly by clause (2).
accepted.tq: Distinguish a constitutional enabling provision from the legislation made under it.
accepted.sec: Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956 and Article 262

accepted.s: Under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, a State seeking adjudication of an inter-State river-water dispute makes a complaint under which section?
accepted.x: A State makes a complaint under Section 3 of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, which provides the basis for constituting a tribunal in the prescribed circumstances.
accepted.tq: Test the exact statutory section, a common article-section confusion point.
accepted.sec: Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956 and Article 262

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the two 1956 laws is correct?
o: The River Boards Act created tribunals, while the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act created permanent river boards.
The Inter-State River Water Disputes Act provides for tribunals, whereas no board has ever been set up under the River Boards Act.
The River Boards Act repealed Article 262 and transferred water to the Union List.
Both laws provide only for advisory councils and neither concerns adjudication.
accepted.x: The Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 provides for tribunals. Although the River Boards Act, 1956 provides a statutory framework for river boards, no board has ever been set up under it.
accepted.tq: Compare the institutional purpose and practical outcome of the two similarly dated Acts.
accepted.sec: Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956 and Article 262

accepted.s: Water is included in Entry 17 of the State List subject to which entry of the Union List?
accepted.x: Water is Entry 17 in the State List, but it is subject to Entry 56 of the Union List concerning the regulation and development of inter-State rivers and river valleys.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the State-List entry and the overriding Union-List entry.
accepted.sec: Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956 and Article 262

accepted.s: The 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council referred to in the context of Krishna and Godavari disputes was held at:
accepted.x: The 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting was held at Mahabalipuram in August 2026 and was chaired by the Union Home Minister.
accepted.tq: Match the meeting number with its place and time rather than the subject of discussion alone.

accepted.s: At the 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting, Telangana sought which combination of measures?
o: A ban on all Godavari projects and abolition of the KRMB
Transfer of the Krishna River to the Union List and cancellation of Polavaram
Protection of its Krishna rights and national-project status for Kaleshwaram and Palamuru-Rangareddy
Exclusive control over Srisailam and operation of Nagarjuna Sagar by the State government
accepted.x: Telangana sought protection of its Krishna rights and national-project status for Kaleshwaram and Palamuru-Rangareddy at the Southern Zonal Council meeting.
accepted.tq: Link the demands to the State that raised them and to the specific projects named.

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes a continuing criticism of the River Management Boards in the Krishna-Godavari context?
o: They exercise exclusive control over all projects in both river basins.
They have full operational control, but no adjudicatory powers at all.
They have been abolished under Article 262(2), leading to disputes only over irrigation.
They still lack full operational control, while disputes over unapproved projects and hydel drawal continue.
accepted.x: The Boards continue to face criticism because they lack full operational control, and disputes concerning unapproved projects and hydel drawal persist.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that captures both the institutional limitation and the continuing sources of dispute.

accepted.s: In the Cauvery water dispute, the Supreme Court’s 2018 verdict fixed the share of Tamil Nadu at:
accepted.x: The 2018 Cauvery verdict fixed Tamil Nadu’s share at 404.25 TMC. Karnataka, Kerala and Puducherry were allocated 284.75, 30 and 7 TMC respectively.
accepted.tq: Separate the largest State share from the other three figures in the comparative allocation.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the Cauvery water shares fixed by the Supreme Court’s 2018 verdict?
o: Tamil Nadu 404.25, Karnataka 284.75, Kerala 7, Puducherry 30 TMC
Tamil Nadu 284.75, Karnataka 404.25, Kerala 30, Puducherry 7 TMC
Tamil Nadu 404.25, Karnataka 284.75, Kerala 30, Puducherry 7 TMC
Tamil Nadu 404.25, Karnataka 30, Kerala 284.75, Puducherry 7 TMC
accepted.x: The comparative allocation was Tamil Nadu 404.25 TMC, Karnataka 284.75 TMC, Kerala 30 TMC and Puducherry 7 TMC.
accepted.tq: Use the fixed numerical sequence to detect swaps among neighbouring States and Union Territories.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements concerning Polavaram:
1. It was declared a national project under Section 90 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act.
2. It is planned to have a generation capacity of 960 MW.
3. Its national-project status was declared under the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
4. Its planned generation capacity is 120 MW.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Polavaram was declared a national project under Section 90 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act and is planned for 960 MW. Statements 3 and 4 are incorrect; 120 MW and the LARR Act, 2013 do not give the stated legal basis or planned capacity.
accepted.tq: Separate the correct statutory basis and capacity from familiar but incorrect alternative details.
